subsystems.name: Probe fleet
subsystems.role: the spacecraft that carry life-seeding payloads across interstellar distances.

subsystems.name: Payload of engineered extremophiles
subsystems.role: organisms designed to survive launch, vacuum, radiation and a hostile new world.
parts: gene circuits for nitrogen fixation and photosynthesis

subsystems.name: Delivery and nutrient package
subsystems.role: gets the microbes onto a surface or into a cloud with the chemistry they need to start.

subsystems.name: Atmosphere and surface engineering
subsystems.role: in theory, warms a target and builds a biosphere over centuries.

subsystems.name: Biosignature monitoring network
subsystems.role: watches whether the seeded life takes hold and spreads.

buildSteps.title: Find and characterise targets
buildSteps.detail: Telescopes identify candidate rogue planets, free-floating worlds and cloud regions, and spectroscopy estimates their temperature, chemistry and radiation.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the microbes
buildSteps.detail: Synthetic-biology techniques add genes for radiation repair, desiccation tolerance, nitrogen fixation and photosynthesis to hardy extremophiles such as radiation-resistant bacteria.

buildSteps.title: Package the payload
buildSteps.detail: Microbes are dried into spores, mixed into a nutrient matrix, and sealed in a capsule that survives vacuum, vibration and decades of cold.

buildSteps.title: Build the probes
buildSteps.detail: Thousands of gram-to-kilogram spacecraft are assembled with automated factories, each carrying a sail or compact propulsion stage and a small sensor suite.

buildSteps.title: Launch and accelerate
buildSteps.detail: A parent craft or ground-based laser array pushes the probes to a few percent of light speed, the approach explored by the Breakthrough Starshot initiative.

buildSteps.title: Cruise and navigate
buildSteps.detail: Decades of autonomous flight, with the fleet steering itself using star trackers and onboard AI.

buildSteps.title: Arrive and seed
buildSteps.detail: Probes release their payload into an atmosphere or onto a surface and begin local atmospheric and nutrient conditioning.

buildSteps.title: Monitor and report
buildSteps.detail: Sensors track biosignatures over years and relay findings back to Earth.

prerequisites.why: laser-driven light sails are studied on paper and in small tests, but nothing has yet been accelerated to a fraction of light speed.
engineered extremophiles exist in labs, but nothing designed to survive interstellar travel and reproduce on an alien world.
a probe must operate for decades with no repair and no real-time control.
signals take years to arrive and weaken enormously; no infrastructure exists for receiving them.
even terraforming one planet is unproven; influencing a whole galaxy is far beyond current capability.

pathway.milestone: characterising exoplanets and rogue planets; cataloguing and engineering extremophiles
pathway.unlocks: the target list and the biological toolkit.

pathway.milestone: directed-panspermia experiments inside the solar system, such as seeding a Mars analogue or a Venus-like cloud
pathway.unlocks: proof that engineered life can survive delivery and establish itself.

pathway.milestone: interstellar precursor probes reaching the nearest stars and returning data
pathway.unlocks: the propulsion and autonomy needed for anything larger.

pathway.milestone: a self-replicating or mass-produced fleet able to seed many systems
pathway.unlocks: a galaxy-spanning biosphere — should physics, biology and ethics ever permit it.
